title: The Teardown 003 — Anthropic's SDLC playbook, minus the AI
description: Anthropic published how it builds software with agents. The reusable part is not the agents: it is that every stage ends by committing a file, so the chain doubles as an audit trail. The headline claim that code is no longer the bottleneck is the part with the least evidence behind it, and the best randomised trial in the field found the opposite.
og_title: Anthropic's playbook, minus the AI — The Teardown 003
og_description: intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, the diff. Six stages, one commit per handoff, and a loop back from production. What holds up, what does not, and the one thing the agent is never allowed to do.
og_alt: The artifact chain: Plan commits intent.md, Design commits spec.md, Build commits plan.md and the diff, Test commits evals, Deploy commits a merged PR behind a human approval gate, Maintain commits an incident record that writes the next intent.md
